t: 井の中の蛙大海を知らず
r: いのなかのかわずたいかいをしらず
mean: someone in a small world who thinks it is the whole world
lit: the frog in the well does not know the great sea

story.text: In the 'Autumn Floods' chapter of the Zhuangzi, the god of the Yellow River is proud of his swollen river until he reaches the sea and sees no end to it. The spirit of the North Sea tells him that you cannot talk about the sea to a frog in a well, because it is confined to its little space. The Japanese saying comes from this image.

use.how: Said of someone whose small surroundings made them overconfident, often of oneself in hindsight; often shortened: 私は井の中の蛙だった。

cue: A boy who was the best player in his small town joins a national academy and finds dozens of players far better than him.

ctx.s: 地元[じもと]の大会[たいかい]で勝[か]っただけで威張[いば]るなんて、{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]大海[たいかい]を知[し]らず}だよ。
ctx.en: Showing off just because you won a local tournament? You're a frog in a well who's never seen the sea.

ctx.s: 留学[りゅうがく]して初[はじ]めて、自分[じぶん]が{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]}だったと気[き]づいた。
ctx.en: It was only when I studied abroad that I realised I had been a frog in a well.

ctx.s: 「{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]}にならないように、いろいろな人[ひと]と話[はな]してみなさい」と先生[せんせい]に言[い]われた。
ctx.en: My teacher told me, "Talk to all kinds of people, so you don't end up a frog in a well."

ctx.s: 社内[しゃない]の常識[じょうしき]だけで判断[はんだん]していたら、{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]}になりませんか。
ctx.en: If we judge everything by our own company's assumptions, won't we become frogs in a well?

ctx.s: 全国大会[ぜんこくたいかい]に出[で]て、彼[かれ]は{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]大海[たいかい]を知[し]らず}という言葉[ことば]の意味[いみ]を思[おも]い知[し]った。
ctx.en: At the national championships he learned the hard way what 'the frog in the well knows nothing of the sea' means.

ctx.s: 国内[こくない]で成功[せいこう]したから海外[かいがい]でも通用[つうよう]すると考[かんが]えるのは、{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]}と言[い]わざるを得[え]ない。
ctx.en: Assuming that success at home means success abroad can only be called the view of a frog in a well.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は駅[えき]までの道[みち]を知[し]らないから、{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]大海[たいかい]を知[し]らず}だ。
bad.en: (meant: he doesn't know the way to the station)
bad.why: It is about a narrow outlook and the overconfidence it breeds, not about simply not knowing one fact.

bad.s: 祖父[そふ]は一生[いっしょう]この村[むら]を愛[あい]し、{井[い]の中[なか]の蛙[かわず]}として幸[しあわ]せに暮[く]らした。
bad.en: (meant: grandfather loved his village and lived there contentedly all his life)
bad.why: It criticises narrow-mindedness; using it to praise a contented local life would insult the grandfather.

t: 三人寄れば文殊の知恵
r: さんにんよればもんじゅのちえ
mean: ordinary people putting their heads together come up with good ideas
lit: when three people gather, they have the wisdom of Monju (Manjushri, the Buddhist bodhisattva of wisdom)

use.how: Quoted to urge or welcome pooling ideas: 〜って言うじゃない, まさに〜だ. Said of ordinary people thinking together, not of one clever person.

near.t: 船頭多くして船山に上る
near.diff: That saying is the opposite warning: with too many people giving orders, a project goes wrong. 三人寄れば文殊の知恵 praises thinking together.

cue: Three classmates stuck on a group project, none of them an expert, decide that if they brainstorm together they will surely think of something.

ctx.s: 一人[ひとり]で悩[なや]まないで、みんなで考[かんが]えようよ。{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}って言[い]うじゃない。
ctx.en: Don't agonise over it alone; let's all think about it together. Two heads are better than one, as they say.

ctx.s: 難[むずか]しい問題[もんだい]も、友達[ともだち]と相談[そうだん]したら解[と]けた。まさに{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}だ。
ctx.en: Even that hard problem got solved once I talked it over with my friends. Two heads really are better than one.

ctx.s: 「{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}だね。こんないい案[あん]が出[で]るとは思[おも]わなかった！」
ctx.en: "Put our heads together and look at that! I never thought we'd come up with such a good idea!"

ctx.s: 専門家[せんもんか]がいなくても、{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}で何[なん]とかなるんじゃないかな。
ctx.en: Even without an expert, if we put our heads together we can probably manage, can't we?

ctx.s: 予算[よさん]が足[た]りず困[こま]っていたが、{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}で、チームは新[あたら]しい方法[ほうほう]を見[み]つけた。
ctx.en: Short of budget, the team was stuck, but by pooling their ideas they found a new way forward.

ctx.s: {三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}と申[もう]しますように、本日[ほんじつ]は皆様[みなさま]の自由[じゆう]なご意見[いけん]をお聞[き]かせください。
ctx.en: As the saying goes, many minds make good ideas, so today please share your views freely.

bad.s: 会議[かいぎ]に人[ひと]が多[おお]すぎて、{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}で何[なに]も決[き]まらなかった。
bad.en: (meant: there were too many people at the meeting, so nothing got decided)
bad.why: It says that gathering produces good ideas; too many voices causing confusion calls for the opposite saying about too many boatmen.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は一人[ひとり]で何[なん]でも解決[かいけつ]できる、{三人[さんにん]寄[よ]れば文殊[もんじゅ]の知恵[ちえ]}のような人[ひと]だ。
bad.en: (meant: he is so clever he can solve anything on his own)
bad.why: It is about the wisdom of a group of ordinary people, not praise for one person's brilliance.
